news.label: Gemini 4 Neon Announced
details: Google DeepMind has announced Gemini 4 Neon, built for complex software development, analysis, and science.
API pricing is 3 dollars per million input tokens and 15 dollars for output.
Google says it also follows corrections given in the middle of a task more closely.

lines.say: First up, Google's new model, Gemini four Neon.
lines.show: First up, Google's new model, Gemini 4 Neon.

lines.say: It has a long one million token context, and it's strong at development and analysis.
lines.show: It has a one million token context and is strong at development and analysis.

lines.say: It even keeps up when you change your instructions midway.
lines.show: It even keeps up when you change your instructions midway.

news.label: MIRACO 2 Unveiled
points: Scan to edit, no PC needed
details: This handheld device handles scanning, point cloud processing, and basic editing without a PC.
The maker says it offers six scan modes and single-frame accuracy of up to 0.02 millimeters.
It assists with scan-to-CAD and inspection tasks using natural language, and supports true-scale 3D Gaussian Splatting when connected to a PC.

lines.say: Next, a three D scanner: Revopoint's Miraco two.
No computer needed. You can go from scanning to editing on this one device.
lines.show: No computer needed. Go from scanning to editing on one device.

lines.say: And you can even ask the AI for help in plain words.
lines.show: And you can even ask the AI for help in plain words.

news.label: Formnext 2026 Award Winners
points: No need to dry whole filament
details: Using CFD simulation and Bayesian optimization, a team developed cAIclone, a 3D-printed hydrocyclone for separating fine particles.
Thought3D's Drywise conditions the humidity of only the necessary section just before the nozzle.
It replaces pre-drying the entire filament, and can make drying more efficient for moisture-prone materials such as nylon.

lines.say: A printed part with AI-optimized flow channels and a device that dries filament just before printing were both honored.

lines.say: It's a clever idea you'll want to try yourself.

news.label: Renesas Five-Finger Robot Hand
points: Grips an egg without breaking it
details: In a demo, the hand picked up items like an egg, a sponge, and a can, using just the right force for each.
It identifies objects through image recognition with the RZ/V2H, then uses fingertip pressure sensors and preset grip forces.
A second demo used another camera to read hand gestures and had the robot hand copy the movements.

lines.say: Next, a robot hand from Renesas.
lines.show: Next, a robot hand from Renesas.

lines.say: In the demo, it picked up an egg, a sponge, and a can, changing its grip force each time.
lines.show: In the demo, it gripped an egg, a sponge, and a can with different force.

lines.say: Combining fingertip sensors with image recognition is a really neat approach.
lines.show: Combining fingertip sensors with image recognition is a neat approach.

news.label: Foundry Dev Pack Now Available
points: Agent dev tools in one install
CLI and plugins set up too
details: A bundled development environment for building, debugging, evaluating, and deploying AI agents is now generally available.
From the Agent Inspector in VS Code, you can examine traces of requests and tool calls.
Along with the CLI (azd ai) and Foundry Skill, it also sets up the VS Code Toolkit and plugins for GitHub Copilot in supported environments.
